name: SLN
author: Soren Nielsen

provenance.from: Ultimate Amiga forum, AMOS Factory downloads section, retrieved 2026-07-26. Most items there are credited "provided and archived by Lonewolf10". Archive path: SLN_Extensions.
provenance.note: Documentation coverage was measured by counting how many of the library's own keyword names appear in the files shipped beside it, taking only files that can be documentation (not disk images, example programs or the library itself). That measures the DOCUMENTATION, which is what the `docs` field records; it does not set the evidence tier, which follows from what is available to read. Here the tier is SOURCE and it is genuinely complete: sln_extII.s holds every routine body, unlike GameSupport.s, which turned out to be the shell only. The binary was still disassembled with `extdis sln-2.0` wherever the source said something surprising, and it agreed every time -- which is how the S Mouse Button and array defects were confirmed to have shipped rather than to be a stale source file.
provenance.redistribution: Third-party extension, redistribution terms unverified unless stated in the notes. Kept as a fixture for identification and reference only.

findings: `S Iinit` is the one keyword approximated here, because its 68k VBL routine cannot be entered in a port that runs no machine code; one other is n/a. `sln_extII.s` is the author's OWN assembler source and for this extension it is the WHOLE thing rather than a shell -- 4,949 lines carrying every routine, the token table, the data zone and the error strings, with nothing in its `include` list but macro and equate files. `ExtNb equ 24-1` is the slot in his own hand, and the binary agrees from the other side: every routine stores through `$268(a5)`, and ExtAdr is $f8 with sixteen bytes a slot, so ($268-$f8)/16+1 = 24. Six groups that have little to do with each other: a mouse counter reader, eight typed arrays outside AMOS's variable system, eight user VBL hooks, a sample player with its own bank format, raw trackdisk.device sector access, and a PT2.3A replayer. NOTE the count: Sln_ext_Historie ends 'indeholder nu ialt 71 kommandoer' where the table has 70 names, and the missing one is `S Mask$` -- in the table as `dc.w 1,-1` with the author's comment 'This command is non-existent!!! DO NOT USE. / Strictly for maintaining compability', padding to keep v1.0 token ids valid. Its spec parses it as a string function and its function routine is -1, so it is n/a. The port pins fourteen defects that shipped, every one confirmed in the binary before it was reproduced; src/runtime/sln.ts and the NOTES in src/coverage/status.ts say which and where.
notes: Mouse control, fast arrays and assorted utilities. Ships with the author's assembler source.
